dispute_description: N.R. Dongre and Others are the registered proprietors of the trademark WHIRLPOOL in India for home appliances, having used the mark since 1955. Whirlpool Corporation, an American multinational, began selling washing machines in India under the WHIRLPOOL mark, relying on transborder reputation acquired through advertisements in international publications widely circulated in India. Whirlpool Corporation contends that Indian consumers associate the WHIRLPOOL mark with its goods due to this transborder reputation, and that N.R. Dongre's use of the same mark for inferior goods in India constitutes passing off of the Corporation's reputation. N.R. Dongre contests this, asserting priority by registration and long prior use in India. The dispute concerns whether Whirlpool Corporation's transborder reputation entitles it to protection against passing off in India independent of registration. No contractual relationship exists between the parties.
